audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL topics including EVM control flow (Prague JUMP/JUMPI/STOP), environment opcodes (Cancun BALANCE/CALLDATALOAD/RETURNDATACOPY/BLOBHASH), BLAKE2b precompile, SSTORE gas metering (EIP-2200), SELFDESTRUCT deprecation (EIP-6049), difficulty bomb delay (EIP-1234), and wallet transaction UX (EIP-2566). CL topics include PeerDAS data availability sampling (EIP-7594). Meta/governance EIPs (EIP-1872, EIP-5069) are noted but have no runtime protocol entities.

in_scope: EVM Control Flow (JUMP, JUMPI, STOP, PC, GAS, JUMPDEST)
EVM Environment Opcodes (BALANCE, CALLDATALOAD, CALLDATACOPY, RETURNDATACOPY, BLOBHASH, BLOBBASEFEE, EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODEHASH)
SSTORE Gas Metering and Reentrancy Guard (EIP-2200)
Column Custody and KZG Proof Verification
Blob Transaction Validation with Cell Proofs
out_of_scope: Beacon Chain state transitions beyond DAS

threats: Spoofed ABI metadata in wallet confirmations (EIP-2566)
Send blocks with incorrect difficulty calculations
Blocks with manipulated SSTORE gas costs
Reentrancy attacks exploiting SSTORE gas changes (EIP-2200)
Column custody manipulation via node ID grinding
Submit blobs with invalid cell proofs

misclassified_entities.reason: EVM Precompile Caller is an internal EVM component. Smart contracts calling precompiles do so through the EVM execution engine, which is internal to the EL. The actual external entity is the transaction sender who triggered the contract execution.
EVM Execution Context is internal to the EL. Contracts calling BLAKE2b do so within an already-validated execution frame. Not an external entity.
Contract Execution Context is internal to the EVM. SSTORE is invoked by already-executing code, not directly by an external entity.

Contract Deployer deploys bytecode via a transaction, but at the point of EVM control flow execution, the deployer has no direct interaction. The transaction sender is the correct external entity; the deployer's influence is mediated through already-validated bytecode.
EIP-1872 is a Meta EIP about governance/scheduling. Core developers are not runtime external entities interacting with the Ethereum protocol at the protocol level.
EIP-1872 governance entity. Not a runtime external entity.
EIP-1872 governance entity. Node operators interact at an operational level, not as protocol-level external data sources.
EIP-5069 governance entity. Editor candidate is a meta-process participant, not a runtime external entity.
EIP-5069 governance entity. Keeper of Consensus is a meta-process role, not a runtime external entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated user or application submitting transactions that trigger EVM execution (SELFDESTRUCT, SSTORE, JUMP, precompile calls, environment opcodes). All transaction data is potentially malicious. Covers EXT-TRANSACTION (EIP-6049), EXT-TRANSACTION-SENDER (Cancun env), EXT-BLOB-TX-SUBMITTER (Cancun blob).

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via eth_sendTransactionToContractFunction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps provide ABI metadata alongside transactions. A malicious DApp can provide a misleading ABI that passes function selector validation but misrepresents the actual contract behavior. The ABI is not verified against on-chain contract code. Covers EXT-DAPP from EIP-2566.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User via UI Confirmation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: End user reviewing transaction details in wallet. User decisions are based on potentially misleading ABI information provided by the DApp. The user is an external entity whose approval triggers transaction submission. Covers EXT-USER from EIP-2566.

trusted_external_entities.name: Reentering Contract via CALL
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM CALL opcode with 2300 gas stipend
trusted_external_entities.rationale: A contract receiving ETH via transfer()/send() gets a 2300 gas stipend and may attempt SSTORE. EIP-2200 explicitly guards against this by failing SSTORE when gasleft <= 2300. The reentering call is untrusted and potentially malicious. Covers EXT-REENTERING-CALL from EIP-2200.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Block Propagation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote nodes propagate blocks containing difficulty values, block rewards, and state transitions. A malicious peer can send blocks with incorrect difficulty calculations (EIP-1234 fake_block_number), wrong reward amounts (2 vs 3 ETH), or invalid state roots. Covers EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER (EIP-1234) and EXT-PEER (EIP-1234).

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Nodes via P2P Column Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network (column gossip subnets, DataColumnSidecar requests per EIP-7594)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes respond to column sampling requests and gossip column data. Malicious peers can withhold data, provide invalid KZG proofs, or attempt eclipse attacks. All received column data must be cryptographically verified. Covers EXT-PEER-NODES and EXT-PEER-CUSTODIANS from EIP-7594.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Transaction Submitter via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network (blob transaction gossip with cell proofs per EIP-7594)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Entities submitting blob transactions with wrapper data including cell proofs. Must validate blob count <= 6, quantity match between versioned hashes/blobs/commitments, cell proof count, KZG hash validity, and batch verify cell proofs. Covers EXT-TX-SUBMITTER and EXT-USER from EIP-7594.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature, nonce, balance, gas limit. Once in EVM: SELFDESTRUCT beneficiary address validation, JUMP/JUMPI destination must be in valid_jump_destinations set, CALLDATALOAD zero-pads out-of-bounds reads, RETURNDATACOPY performs bounds checking (OutOfBoundsRead exception), BLOBHASH returns zero for invalid indices, BLAKE2b precompile validates input length and final flag (0 or 1).

Wallet MUST validate that ABI-derived function selector (keccak256 first 4 bytes) matches transaction data prefix. ABI mismatch must be rejected or warned. Even with matching selectors, wallet must communicate that displayed information originates from the DApp, not from verified contract code. Function selector collisions are possible.
Wallet must clearly present that ABI information is DApp-provided and unverified. User approval triggers transaction submission. Rejection must prevent submission. No automatic approval permitted.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM SSTORE opcode (EIP-2200 gas stipend check)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: SSTORE MUST fail with OOG exception when gasleft <= 2300. This prevents reentrancy attacks where a contract called via transfer()/send() with only the 2300 gas stipend attempts state modifications. The gas check must occur BEFORE any gas metering logic.

Block difficulty must be recalculated and verified: post-Constantinople blocks must use fake_block_number = max(0, block.number - 5000000). Block reward must be exactly 2 ETH base (post-Constantinople) with correct nephew/uncle calculations. Uncle reward formula ((8-k) * base_reward) / 8 must be verified. Gas metering for SSTORE must follow EIP-2200 net gas rules.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P column gossip subnets / DataColumnSidecar RPC (EIP-7594)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All received column samples must have KZG proofs batch-verified against commitments. Custody column assignment must be deterministic from node ID and not manipulable. Sufficient column diversity (>= 50% for reconstruction) must be ensured. Peer discovery must maintain diverse connections to prevent eclipse attacks on specific columns.

Blob count <= 6. Equal quantities of versioned_hashes, blobs, commitments. Cell proof count == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB * len(blobs). KZG commitments must hash to versioned hashes. All cell proofs must pass batch verification. Wrapper version must be 1 for PeerDAS format.
